summary: On Wednesday, October 14, 2026, the Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027, affecting more than 76 million Americans. This annual adjustment aims to help beneficiaries manage rising prices for essential goods and services.

The 3.6% figure derives from the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers , which tracked average price changes from July through September 2026. This metric measures inflation across a basket of goods purchased by workers.

Retirees will receive an average monthly payment increase of $75 in 2027. The projected Medicare Part B premium increase of just $6.60 suggests many seniors may retain more of this year's COLA than in recent years.

Senior advocacy groups argue this adjustment fails to restore lost purchasing power. AARP CEO Myechia Minter-Jordan noted that one in five older Americans lacks retirement savings, intensifying financial insecurity amid persistent inflation.

Without legislative reform, the Old Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund faces depletion by 2032. Experts warn this could trigger a 22% payment cut for beneficiaries, a long-standing concern for the system's long-term viability.
title: Social Security Administration announces 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027

Expanded Chinese production would help Solidigm fund a U.S. NAND plant, and the company is considering an initial public offering as early as next year to finance this facility.

summary: On Oct. 9, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed a lawsuit in Collin County against Gerber Products and Nestlé, alleging the companies misled Texans about baby food safety and testing.
Paxton alleges Gerber marketed products as safe and rigorously tested despite internal tests revealing toxic metals including arsenic, lead, cadmium and mercury in the ingredients.
Tests revealed Gerber carrots contained up to 17 times the bottled-water limit for cadmium, while sweet potatoes had nearly 10 times the limit for lead from 2017 through 2019.

Suing under the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act, the state seeks civil penalties exceeding $10 million; Competitor Beech-Nut previously recalled infant rice cereal after similar arsenic findings, unlike Gerber.

Gerber began posting test results via QR codes in 2025 to comply with California law, but the lawsuit argues these do not resolve the alleged deception since Gerber has not issued a recall for heavy metals.

summary: On Wednesday, the Supreme Court heard oral arguments in Salazar v. Paramount Global, examining whether the 1988 Video Privacy Protection Act applies to digital tracking tools used by modern media companies.

Congress enacted the Video Privacy Protection Act in 1988 after Supreme Court nominee Robert Bork's rental history leaked to the press. Salazar alleges Paramount violated this law by sharing his Facebook ID and video-watching history with Facebook without consent.

At issue is whether Salazar qualifies as a 'consumer' under the statute. Paramount argues the law covers only those purchasing audiovisual materials, while Salazar contends it broadly protects anyone subscribing to any service from a video provider.

During arguments, Justice Elana Kagan stressed companies could easily obtain consent or use paywalls. Paramount lawyer Paul Clement countered that broad interpretations would create "unworkable" liabilities for routine digital business practices.

A ruling expected by next summer could resolve a circuit split over the law's scope. The outcome may reshape how companies use tracking technologies for targeted advertising, potentially exposing businesses to significant liability.
title: Supreme Court weighs scope of 1980s video privacy law in internet newsletter age

summary: On Tuesday, Georgia began early voting for the midterm election with more than 188,600 in-person ballots cast on the first day, breaking the midterm early voting record.
The first-day total represents a 40 percent increase from the 134,962 ballots cast in 2022, and exceeds the 70,849 voters recorded during the 2018 midterm's first day.
Officials have accepted 10,267 absentee ballots out of more than 130,000 issued, while voters now complete an additional check-in step requiring poll workers to handwrite names on numbered lists.

Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger attributed the turnout to voter confidence in election integrity, stating, "This record-breaking turnout proves that voters have confidence in the integrity of our elections."
Early voting continues through Oct. 30, with Election Day scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3. Voters can find polling locations through the Secretary of State's Voter Page.
title: Georgia shatters its Day 1 early voting record for a midterm

summary: On Tuesday, the Pentagon appointed Christian Devine, an executive director and principal adviser in its public affairs office, as acting publisher of Stars and Stripes. Devine will retain his Pentagon duties while leading the publication until a permanent replacement is hired.

This appointment follows an internal overhaul initiated by chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell in January to remove "woke distractions." The department previously dismissed editor-in-chief Erik Slavin, reporter Lara Korte, publisher Max Lederer, and ombudsman Jacqueline Smith.

Lawmakers, including Sen. Elizabeth Warren, allege recent Pentagon actions threaten the paper's editorial independence. U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta warned that standard rules could make First Amendment protections "a hollow promise for Stars and Stripes journalists."

Devine acknowledged he has "a lot to learn" about his new role but expressed commitment to preserving editorial integrity. He said he is "confident that Stripes can modernize its platform to prioritize original reporting" relevant to the military community.

title: Pentagon taps DOD public affairs official as Stars and Stripes publisher

summary: On Wednesday, the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that Florida's law banning social media accounts for minors is likely constitutional, reversing a lower court's preliminary injunction. The decision allows House Bill 3 to remain in effect while legal challenges proceed.

Signed by Governor Ron DeSantis in 2024, the law prohibits children under 14 from creating personal accounts and mandates parental permission for 14- and 15-year-olds. It targets platforms utilizing algorithms and 'addictive features' like infinite scrolling to engage young users.

A unanimous three-judge panel applied intermediate scrutiny, concluding the statute is content-neutral because it regulates platform mechanics rather than specific viewpoints. The court noted the law 'doesn't burden substantially more speech than necessary' to protect minors from social media addiction.

NetChoice and the Computer & Communications Industry Association criticized the ruling, with director Paul Taske warning it could force social media sites to verify the age and parental status of all users. The groups alleged this creates compliance burdens.

While the legal challenges continue in district court, the law remains in effect across Florida. Several other states have implemented similar restrictions on youth social media access, which are also currently facing active legal challenges in court.
title: Florida wins key ruling allowing it to enforce a law that targets social media use by kids

summary: The San Francisco Police Department announced the arrest of four suspects on Wednesday in connection with the February 9 shooting of 49ers defensive end Keion White at a Mission District nightclub.
Early on February 9, White was shot in the ankle at the Dahlia Lounge after an argument involving rapper Lil Baby's entourage escalated, according to police reports.

San Francisco Police Chief Derrick Lew said the months-long 'Operation D-Line' involved over 250 law enforcement personnel and 50 search warrants, resulting in seizure of firearms and nearly 15 pounds of narcotics.
Gregory Walker and Curtis Green were booked into San Francisco County Jail on Monday, while authorities work to transfer Marquis Davis and Antoine Washington to San Francisco to face charges.
After undergoing successful surgery, White returned to the field this season and has recorded 3.0 sacks in four of the 49ers' five games while maintaining a career-best pace.
title: 4 arrested in the shooting of San Francisco 49ers player Keion White at a Super Bowl party

summary: On Wednesday, Luna, a 10-year-old Jack Russell terrier, was reunited with her California owners after spending over a month lost in Yellowstone National Park .
A housekeeping staffer accidentally opened a cabin door, causing Luna to bolt into the sprawling 3,500-square-mile park home to grizzly bears, wolves and other predators.

Katie Boucher, president of the Norris Ark Training and Recovery Center in Norris, Montana, set a trap baited with family-scented items as Luna had been spotted retracing her family's steps through lodges and employee housing.
A veterinary examination on Wednesday afternoon found Luna underweight but alert and in good spirits, according to Boucher.
Rescue efforts intensified as winter approached and the seasonal RV park where Luna stayed prepared to close next Monday, with local resident Marie Jaskula urging visitors not to chase the dog.
title: Luna, a small dog missing for over a month in Yellowstone, is reunited with her owners

Forming the International Stabilization Force, the proposed 100-meter-by-100-meter compound would accommodate approximately 150 troops drawn from a 500-soldier contingent supplied by Morocco and Kosovo.
Without this base, the broader reconstruction pilot in Rafah cannot proceed, as the stabilization force is required to provide security for construction crews installing utilities and infrastructure.
